lunda-empire.name: Lunda Empire
lunda-empire.summary: A confederation of states centered in Katanga, spanning parts of today's Democratic Republic of Congo, Angola and Zambia.

khoisan.name: Khoisan
khoisan.summary: An umbrella term for Southern Africa's non-Bantu indigenous peoples, combining the Khoekhoen and Sān, who speak click languages and descend from some of the earliest modern human populations in the region.

bantu-peoples.name: Bantu peoples
bantu-peoples.summary: An ethnolinguistic grouping of about 400 African ethnic groups speaking Bantu languages, including large groups such as the Zulu, Shona and Xhosa.

columbian-exchange.name: Columbian exchange
columbian-exchange.summary: The widespread transfer of plants, animals and diseases between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia beginning in the late 15th century, named for Christopher Columbus.

luba-empire.name: Luba Empire
luba-empire.summary: Pre-colonial Central African state centered in the Upemba Depression of what is now southern DR Congo.

mutapa-empire.name: Mutapa Empire
mutapa-empire.summary: A Shona empire on the northern Zimbabwean Plateau, also called Mwenemutapa or Monomotapa, whose ruler's title meant 'Lord of the Conquered Land' and came to name the whole kingdom.

cape-malays.name: Cape Malays
cape-malays.summary: An ethnic group in South Africa descended from enslaved and free Muslims brought mainly from the Dutch East Indies, whose culture shaped Cape Town cuisine and written Afrikaans.

prazo.name: Prazo
prazo.summary: A large estate in Portuguese Africa leased to colonists and traders to exploit local resources, functioning as a semi-feudal entity mainly in the Zambezi River valley.

huguenots.name: Huguenots
huguenots.summary: French Protestants of the Reformed Calvinist tradition, concentrated in southern and western France, who made up about 10% of the population before the St. Bartholomew's Day massacre of 1572 and faced later persecution under Louis XIV.

franschhoek.name: Franschhoek
franschhoek.summary: Small town in South Africa's Western Cape, about 75 km from Cape Town, one of the country's oldest towns, once named for elephants that roamed its valley.

kuba-kingdom.name: Kuba Kingdom
kuba-kingdom.summary: Traditional kingdom in Central Africa that flourished from the 17th to 19th centuries, uniting many ethnic groups under a ruler called the nyim.

giovanni-cavazzi-da-montecuccolo.name: Giovanni Antonio Cavazzi da Montecuccolo
giovanni-cavazzi-da-montecuccolo.summary: Italian Capuchin missionary priest (1621–1678) who traveled in Portuguese Angola and wrote a lengthy account of local history, culture and the Capuchin mission there.

kingdom-of-kongo.name: Kingdom of Kongo
kingdom-of-kongo.summary: A Central African kingdom spanning parts of modern Angola, Congo and Gabon, independent from around 1390 to 1862, later a Portuguese vassal until its monarchy was abolished in 1914.

manuel-i-of-portugal.name: Manuel I of Portugal
manuel-i-of-portugal.summary: King of Portugal from 1495 to 1521, known as the Fortunate, whose reign saw major overseas expansion including Vasco da Gama's sea route to India and Cabral's discovery of Brazil.

great-zimbabwe.name: Great Zimbabwe
great-zimbabwe.summary: A city in south-eastern Zimbabwe settled around 1000 AD, capital of the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe from the 13th century and the largest stone structure in precolonial Southern Africa, built by ancestors of the Shona people.

sofala.name: Sofala
sofala.summary: A historic Swahili city-state on the coast of Mozambique, first used as a port by Mogadishan merchants and known as a hub of the gold trade.

m-banza-kongo.name: Mbanza Kongo
m-banza-kongo.summary: Capital of the Kingdom of Kongo from before Portuguese contact in 1483 until 1915; now a city in Angola and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2017.

nzambi-ampungu.name: Nzambi Ampungu
nzambi-ampungu.summary: The Supreme God and eternal Sky Father of traditional Kongo spirituality, associated with the sun; his female counterpart rules the moon. After Portuguese colonization he became identified with the Christian God.

battle-of-salt-river.name: Battle of Salt River
battle-of-salt-river.summary: Small clash between a Portuguese fleet led by Francisco de Almeida and the indigenous ǃUriǁʼaekua. It was the first military encounter between Europeans and indigenous people in what became South Africa.

kingdom-of-ndongo.name: Kingdom of Ndongo
kingdom-of-ndongo.summary: An early-modern African kingdom between the Lukala and Kwanza rivers in what is now Angola, first recorded in the 1500s as a vassal of Kongo and ruled by a king called the Ngola.

kingdom-of-matamba.name: Kingdom of Matamba
kingdom-of-matamba.summary: An African state in what is now Angola from before 1550 to 1744, joined with Ndongo by Queen Nzinga in 1631, that long resisted Portuguese colonization.

dutch-west-india-company.name: Dutch West India Company
dutch-west-india-company.summary: Dutch chartered company founded in 1621, given a monopoly on trade and colonisation across West Africa and the Americas, including a role in the Atlantic slave trade.

battle-of-mbwila.name: Battle of Mbwila
battle-of-mbwila.summary: A 29 October 1665 battle in which Portuguese forces defeated the Kingdom of Kongo and beheaded King António I, also called Nvita a Nkanga.

ant-nio-i-of-kongo.name: António I of Kongo
ant-nio-i-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1661, killed and defeated at the Battle of Mbwila in 1665 while pursuing a policy of removing the Portuguese from the region.

nzinga-of-ndongo-and-matamba.name: Nzinga
nzinga-of-ndongo-and-matamba.summary: Queen of the Ambundu kingdoms of Ndongo (1624–1663) and Matamba (1631–1663) in present-day Angola, trained from childhood in military and political affairs and skilled as a diplomat.

kinlaza.name: Kinlaza
kinlaza.summary: One of the ruling houses of the Kingdom of Kongo in the 17th century, a leading faction in the Kongo Civil War alongside the Kimpanzu and Kinkanga a Mvika houses.

kimpanzu.name: Kimpanzu
kimpanzu.summary: One of the royal lineages, or houses, from which the kings of Kongo were chosen from the 17th century onward, after Kongo's reunification.

songye-people.name: Songye people
songye-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group of the central Democratic Republic of the Congo, divided into 34 societies each led by a chief, traditionally known as farmers.

upemba-depression.name: Upemba Depression
upemba-depression.summary: A large marshy basin in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with about fifty lakes, populated since the 5th century AD and considered the origin of the Kingdom of Luba.

jan-van-riebeeck.name: Jan van Riebeeck
jan-van-riebeeck.summary: Dutch merchant and colonial administrator (1619–1677) who served as the first Commander of the Cape, from 1652 to 1662.

fort-of-good-hope.name: Fort of Good Hope
fort-of-good-hope.summary: First military building erected in what is now Cape Town, built in 1652. It remained in use until 1674, when the Castle of Good Hope superseded it.

castle-of-good-hope.name: Castle of Good Hope
castle-of-good-hope.summary: Pentagonal 17th-century fort in Cape Town, South Africa, once on the Table Bay shore and now inland. Declared a historical monument in 1936, it is the best-preserved Dutch East India Company fort.

muxima.name: Muxima
muxima.summary: Town on Angola's Kwanza River, occupied by the Portuguese in 1589, who built a church and fortress there by 1599. Its name means "heart" in Kimbundu, and it is the site of a Marian shrine.

benguela.name: Benguela
benguela.summary: A city in western Angola and capital of Benguela Province, one of the country's most populous cities.

luanda.name: Luanda
luanda.summary: Capital and largest city of Angola, founded by the Portuguese in 1576, which served as a center of the slave trade to Brazil before it was prohibited.

salvador-de-s.name: Salvador Correia de Sá
salvador-de-s.summary: A Portuguese admiral and colonial administrator (1594-1688) who fought the Dutch in Brazil in 1625 and recaptured Angola and São Tomé from them in 1647, later governing Rio de Janeiro and Angola.

battle-of-mbanda-kasi.name: Battle of Mbanda Kasi
battle-of-mbanda-kasi.summary: A 1622-23 battle between Portuguese Angola and the Kingdom of Kongo that turned the war in Kongo's favor, ousting Angola's Portuguese governor and freeing enslaved Kongolese captives.

pedro-ii-of-kongo.name: Pedro II of Kongo
pedro-ii-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1622 to 1624, a descendant of King Afonso I, who reigned during Kongo's first conflict with the Portuguese.

battle-of-mbumbi.name: Battle of Mbumbi
battle-of-mbumbi.summary: A 1622 battle in which Portuguese forces defeated the Kingdom of Kongo, spurring Kongo's later drive to expel the Portuguese from its territory.

states-general-of-the-netherlands.name: States General of the Netherlands
states-general-of-the-netherlands.summary: The supreme legislature of the Netherlands, originating in the 15th century, which became the ruling authority of the Dutch Republic after its 1581 split from Spain.

afonso-i-of-kongo.name: Afonso I of Kongo
afonso-i-of-kongo.summary: Sixth ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo, reigning from 1509 to 1542 or 1543; a devout Catholic convert who centralized royal power, expanded the kingdom through war, and deepened ties with Portugal.

jos-i-of-kongo.name: José I of Kongo
jos-i-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1779 to 1785, first of the Kinlaza branch from the southeast. He won a decisive battle outside São Salvador against a rival house, and was succeeded by his brother Afonso V.

john-thornton-historian.name: John Thornton
john-thornton-historian.summary: American historian (born 1949) at Boston University specializing in African, African Diaspora and Atlantic World history.

battle-of-kombi.name: Battle of Kombi
battle-of-kombi.summary: 1647 battle during the Dutch period of Angolan history, won by the Dutch and their allies though they failed to drive the Portuguese from their forts.

garcia-ii-of-kongo.name: Garcia II of Kongo
garcia-ii-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1641 to 1660, seen by some as its greatest king for his piety and his near-expulsion of the Portuguese from Angola, though he also took part in the slave trade.

soyo.name: Soyo
soyo.summary: A city and former independent state in Angola at the mouth of the Congo River, historically significant in conflicts among the Kingdom of Kongo, Portugal and the Dutch.

lvaro-i-of-kongo.name: Álvaro I of Kongo
lvaro-i-of-kongo.summary: King of Kongo from 1568 to 1587 and founder of the Kwilu dynasty.

lu-s-lopes-de-sequeira.name: Luís Lopes de Sequeira
lu-s-lopes-de-sequeira.summary: A military commander in Portuguese Angola who died in 1681.

kingdom-of-libolo.name: Kingdom of Libolo
kingdom-of-libolo.summary: A pre-colonial African kingdom on the Cuanza river in what is now Angola, with governors called hango; it briefly expanded north in the 1500s before Portuguese attacks weakened it in the 1600s.

pedro-iii-of-kongo.name: Pedro III of Kongo
pedro-iii-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo (1648–1680) during its civil war period, elder brother of King João II and a partisan of the House of Kinlaza.

daniel-i-of-kongo.name: Daniel I of Kongo
daniel-i-of-kongo.summary: Ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1674 to 1678, during its civil war between rival royal houses; he died in 1678.

ana-afonso-de-le-o.name: Ana Afonso de Leão
ana-afonso-de-le-o.summary: Queen regnant of the Kingdom of Nkondo from 1673 to 1710, who conquered territories in the Kingdom of Kongo region and was a decisive figure in the Kongolese civil war.

kongo-language.name: Kikongo
kongo-language.summary: A Bantu language of the Kongo people spoken by around seven million people in Central Africa, historically carried across the Atlantic by enslaved Africans.

order-of-friars-minor-capuchin.name: Capuchins
order-of-friars-minor-capuchin.summary: Members of a Franciscan religious order that split off in 1525 to return to a stricter, poorer way of life following the original rule of Francis of Assisi.

antonio-zucchelli.name: Antonio Zucchelli
antonio-zucchelli.summary: Italian Capuchin friar and missionary (1663–1716) best known for his missionary work in the Kingdom of Kongo, on which he published memoirs in 1712.

bantu-languages.name: Bantu languages
bantu-languages.summary: A family of roughly 600 languages spoken by about 350 million people across Central, Southern and Eastern Africa, of which Swahili is the most widely spoken.

kingdom-of-loango.name: Kingdom of Loango
kingdom-of-loango.summary: A Kongo-founded state on Africa's Atlantic coast from roughly the 1500s to 1800s, exporting copper and cloth, at its height reaching from Cape St Catherine near the Congo River's mouth.

description-of-africa-dapper-book.name: Description of Africa
description-of-africa-dapper-book.summary: A 1668 Dutch ethnographic book by geographer Olfert Dapper, describing the parts of Africa known to Europeans at the time.

nkisi.name: Nkisi
nkisi.summary: Spirits, or objects believed to house them, used across the Congo Basin in Central Africa, thought to contain spiritual power; the concept traveled to the Americas with the Atlantic slave trade.

luba-people.name: Luba people
luba-people.summary: Bantu ethnic group of south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo. They built a society by about the 400s CE and later formed a community in the Upemba Depression.

abraham-ortelius.name: Abraham Ortelius
abraham-ortelius.summary: Cartographer and geographer from Antwerp (1527–1598), creator of the first modern atlas, the Theatrum Orbis Terrarum, and the first to propose that the continents had once been joined.

dutch-east-india-company.name: Dutch East India Company
dutch-east-india-company.summary: Dutch trading company founded in 1602 with a monopoly on Asian trade, holding quasi-governmental powers and considered by some the world's first multinational corporation.

batavia-dutch-east-indies.name: Batavia
batavia-dutch-east-indies.summary: A Dutch colonial port city founded in 1619 on the site of Jayakarta, on the location of modern Jakarta, which served for about 320 years as capital of the Dutch East Indies.

kirstenbosch-national-botanical-garden.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
kirstenbosch-national-botanical-garden.summary: Botanical garden at the eastern foot of Table Mountain in Cape Town. Founded in 1913, it was the first in the world dedicated to preserving a country's native flora, and is known for its proteas.

kasanje-kingdom.name: Kasanje
kasanje-kingdom.summary: A Central African kingdom (1620–1910), also called the Jaga Kingdom, founded by an Imbangala mercenary band that had deserted Portuguese ranks and settled on the upper Kwango River.

pende-people.name: Pende
pende-people.summary: An ethnic group of over 250,000 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, known for their distinctive art and divided into Eastern and Western cultural branches.

manyika-kingdom.name: Manyika kingdom
manyika-kingdom.summary: A precolonial state in modern Zimbabwe and Mozambique, founded around 1500 as a vassal of the Mutapa Empire and known for its gold production, later partitioned between Portugal and Britain in 1890.

rozvi-empire.name: Rozvi Empire
rozvi-empire.summary: A Shona state on the Zimbabwean Plateau (c. 1683–1866) established by Changamire Dombo, whose name reflects a legacy as a warrior nation; it became the most powerful fighting force in Zimbabwe.

table-bay.name: Table Bay
table-bay.summary: Natural bay on the Atlantic Ocean at the northern end of the Cape Peninsula, overlooked by Cape Town. It is named after the flat-topped Table Mountain that dominates it.

nsundi.name: Nsundi
nsundi.summary: A former province of the Kingdom of Kongo, with its capital near the Inkisi River in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo.

hari-a-kiluanje.name: Hari a Kiluanje
hari-a-kiluanje.summary: Ambundu tribal lord of Ndongo and claimant to its throne who opposed King Ngola Mbandi and backed the 1617 Portuguese invasion of the kingdom.

pedro-i-of-kongo.name: Pedro I of Kongo
pedro-i-of-kongo.summary: Manikongo (ruler) of the Kingdom of Kongo from 1543 until being deposed in 1545.

diogo-i-nkumbi-a-mpudi.name: Diogo I Nkumbi a Mpudi
diogo-i-nkumbi-a-mpudi.summary: King of Kongo (manikongo) from 1545 to 1561 who won the throne by overthrowing his uncle Pedro Nkanga a Mvemba and later expelled Portuguese residents from the kingdom in 1555.

mwene-muji.name: Mwene Muji
mwene-muji.summary: A polity proposed by historian John Thornton around Lake Mai-Ndombe in the Congo Basin, ruled by the BaNunu, that declined through the 17th to 19th centuries before Belgian conquest.

boma-kingdom.name: Boma Kingdom
boma-kingdom.summary: A 17th-century kingdom of the Boma people around Lake Mai-Ndombe in the Congo Basin, said in the 1640s to control fifteen subordinate kings and become one of the region's mightiest powers.

filippo-pigafetta.name: Filippo Pigafetta
filippo-pigafetta.summary: A Venetian mathematician and explorer (1533-1604) whose 1591 book on the Kingdom of Congo, based on a Portuguese trader's account, was translated into several European languages.

kimpa-vita.name: Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita
kimpa-vita.summary: Kongolese prophetess (1684–1706) who led the Christian movement Antonianism, teaching that Jesus and other early Christian figures came from the Kongo Kingdom, and is remembered as an early antislavery figure.

anthony-of-padua.name: Anthony of Padua
anthony-of-padua.summary: Portuguese Catholic priest and friar (1195–1231) of the Order of Friars Minor.

antonianism.name: Antonianism
antonianism.summary: A syncretic Bakongo Catholic movement formed in the Kingdom of Kongo between 1704 and 1708, founded by Beatriz Kimpa Vita, who claimed possession by Saint Anthony of Padua; she was later burned as a heretic.

kongo-people.name: Kongo people
kongo-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group and speakers of Kikongo who lived along the Atlantic coast in the kingdoms of Kongo, Loango and Kakongo, and were among the first Africans to meet Portuguese traders in 1483.

nganga.name: Nganga
nganga.summary: A spiritual healer, diviner and ritual specialist in traditional Kongo religion, also found among descendants of Kongo and Mbundu peoples across the African diaspora, including Brazil, Cuba and Haiti.

kongo-cosmogram.name: Dikenga (Kongo cosmogram)
kongo-cosmogram.summary: A core symbol of Kongo religion showing the physical and spiritual worlds, the sun's rotation, and the four stages of life, drawn as a cross within a circle.

pedro-iv-of-kongo.name: Pedro IV of Kongo
pedro-iv-of-kongo.summary: King of Kongo who ruled from 1695 to 1718 (effectively from 1709), noted for restoring the country and ending the civil war that had raged since 1666.

nkondi.name: Nkondi
nkondi.summary: Mystical statuettes made by the Kongo people, considered an aggressive subclass of minkisi.

baphia-nitida.name: Tukula (camwood)
baphia-nitida.summary: A red dye and powder made from the bark and heartwood of Baphia nitida (camwood), a hard-wooded tree from central west Africa also used in soaps and skin treatments.

jo-o-i-of-kongo.name: João I of Kongo
jo-o-i-of-kongo.summary: João I of Kongo: Fifth ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo (1470–1509), born Nzinga-a-Nkuwu; he converted to Catholicism after Portuguese sailors arrived, taking the name João, but abandoned the faith in 1495, partly over its requirement of monogamy.
